findings.text: Modern semaphore control syscall entry receives set identifier plus index plus command plus argument and forwards them with a fixed 64 bit version selector to the in file dispatcher.
Legacy semaphore control entry receives the same four syscall arguments and first normalizes the command encoding to derive a version selector before delegating to the shared dispatcher.

32 bit compatibility semaphore control entry receives narrowed argument and forwards with fixed 64 bit version selector to a compatibility dispatcher that converts the narrowed value to a full user pointer and masks the version bit before routing.
Legacy compatibility entry normalizes the command encoding with a compatibility parser to obtain a version selector and then delegates to the compatibility dispatcher.
Semaphore operation entries provide untimed plus 64 bit timed plus 32 bit timed and compatibility timed variants that all converge on a common internal operation routine with an optional timeout.
Two non static helpers expose version aware semaphore control for native and compatibility callers by parsing the command encoding and delegating to the corresponding dispatcher.
Three non static helpers expose semaphore array operations with optional timeout handling for native 64 bit plus compatibility 32 bit and direct in kernel callers.
Two non static helpers expose undo list management for task creation and task exit so clone and exit paths can share or drain per task adjustment state.

Compatibility semaphore descriptor holds a compatibility permission block plus 32 bit old style operation and change times plus four narrowed pointers for internal queue links plus a 16 bit count of semaphores in the set.

Kernel shared memory descriptor holds permission state plus backing file reference plus attach count plus segment size plus attach detach and change times plus creator and last operation process references plus memory lock accounting plus creator task link plus creator list plus owning namespace and uses randomized layout.

Shared memory file context holds numeric identifier plus owning namespace plus backing file plus vector of memory operations and is reachable through the generic file private pointer with separate file and memory operation tables declared elsewhere.
Flag SHM_DEST requests destruction after last detach and equals octal 01000 while flag SHM_LOCKED requests exemption from swapping and equals octal 02000.

User to kernel descriptor copy honors version selector IPC_64 copying full structure while version IPC_OLD copies smaller structure then carries over only ownership and mode while other versions fail and user faults are reported distinctly from invalid versions.

Compatibility converters clear the destination then translate only permission state on input and on output emit permission state plus split 64 bit times into low and high halves for the 64 bit form or truncated times for the old form plus the semaphore count.

Native and compatibility dispatchers reject negative identifiers and resolve caller namespace from current task state, route info selectors IPC_INFO with SEM_INFO to info handling and status selectors IPC_STAT with SEM_STAT and SEM_STAT_ANY to status handling with user copy back, direct array and value selectors GETALL with GETVAL with GETPID with GETNCNT with GETZCNT with SETALL to array handling, handle SETVAL separately, and send IPC_SET with IPC_RMID to the down path while unknown selectors fail as invalid.

Removal and permission update path serializes identifier table access with a write guard while holding a read side critical section during lookup and permission checks, then takes the array guard before destroying or mutating, releasing in reverse order with a special unlock path for destruction.

User operation vector handling validates count bounds against namespace limits, uses on stack storage for small vectors and dynamic storage for large ones, copies the vector from user space, delegates to the core routine, and releases dynamic storage only when used.

Core operation validates vector length and identifier, enforces namespace maximum, checks timeout well formedness when present, derives undo and modify intents and duplicate access hints from flags and opcodes, verifies index range and read versus alter rights and mandatory access approval before locking.

After validation the core attempts immediate atomic completion with timestamp and wakeup updates on success. When blocking is required it enqueues on per semaphore or global pending lists with complex operation tracking, sleeps interruptibly with absolute timeout, revalidates liveness after wakeup, and distinguishes completion from signal interruption and timeout expiry with cleanup of the queue link on interruption.

Undo allocation reuses an existing per process entry when present and otherwise sizes from the live array, pins the array, allocates a variable length adjustment record, relocks and revalidates, discards on race when another thread created the entry, and otherwise links the new record into both process and array lists.
Undo list search requires the list spin guard for mutation and promotion to most recent, allows read side traversal with lock state assertion, and moves a hit to the head while holding the guard.
Clone handling shares the caller undo list with an added reference when the System V semaphore sharing flag is set and otherwise starts the child with no list, propagating allocation failure.

Exit handling detaches the task list and proceeds only for the last reference, then iteratively takes the next adjustment record, skips entries invalidated by removal, locks and revalidates the array, unlinks from both lists, applies adjustments clamped within zero and maximum with process identity update, wakes waiters, and defers record reclamation before freeing the list container.

Status display enters a compatibility mode for array locking, samples operation time under protection, emits key and identifier and mode and count and munged ownership and creator identities and operation and change times in a fixed column order, then attempts to leave compatibility mode.

Shared memory removal privatizes the key and marks pending destruction when attachments remain and otherwise tears down immediately by detaching the backing file, unaccounting pages, removing creator and identifier links, unlocking, releasing memory lock accounting except for huge pages, dropping references and clearing process identities.
Shared memory unlock releases the permission object guard associated with the descriptor.

Value setting interprets the syscall argument differently by platform width and byte order, taking the upper half on big endian 64 bit and the full value elsewhere, while the compatibility path uses the narrowed integer directly, creating truncation risk if callers assume uniform layout.

Semaphore identifiers may be recycled after removal so callers must revalidate liveness after locking and treat an invalidated undo marker as a removal race rather than proceeding with stale adjustment state.
